_meta.description: L15: data-tied numerical claim check. Each entry binds a numerical claim that appears in paper/main.tex to a value derivable from a tracked source file (typically JSON). The check loads the source, evaluates the declared value expression against the loaded object (bound as `d`), and compares to the declared expected value within tolerance. If they diverge, either the paper text or the source data is stale; the cert fails until reconciled. This complements L9 (formula-vs-value math identity for curated relations) by handling arbitrary numerical claims grounded in repo data rather than in formulas.
_meta.value_expr_contract: Python expression evaluated with restricted globals against the loaded source object bound as `d`. Allowed builtins: sum, len, min, max, abs, round, int, float. Allowed names: math (module). Expression must return a number.
_meta.tolerance_contract: Absolute tolerance for numerical comparison. Use 0 for integer counts, 0.5 for percent-rounded-to-int, 1e-3 for ratios.
